subject: Copywriting
title: Social Proof in Email
description: Learn Social Proof in Email in one minute.

hook.text: 'Join 50,000 subscribers' in a signup form increases conversions by 20%. Social proof works before the first email.

buildup.text: Inside emails, social proof takes many forms: customer counts, testimonial quotes, star ratings, press logos.

discovery.text: A single testimonial in a sales email can boost click-through by 25%. Real words from real people beat any headline.

twist.text: The number must be credible. '1 million happy customers' feels inflated. '47,312 subscribers' feels precise and real.

climax.text: The most powerful email social proof: 'Your colleague Sarah just joined.' Peer influence beats crowd influence.

punchline.text: 47,312 subscribers. Precise numbers build more trust than round ones.

quiz.question: How much can a testimonial in a sales email boost click-through?

details.summary: Social proof in emails uses customer reviews, testimonials, subscriber counts, and user statistics to build credibility. Including proof elements like '50,000 customers trust us' or a customer quote increases click-through rates by up to 15%. The brain trusts the crowd's judgment as a shortcut...
details.whyItMatters: Social proof reduces the perceived risk of taking action. In an inbox full of claims, showing that real people have already benefited provides the credibility needed to convert skeptics.
takeaways: Social proof in emails can increase click rates by up to 15%
Customer testimonials are more credible than brand claims
Specific numbers outperform vague assertions of popularity

faq.question: What types of social proof work best in emails?
faq.answer: Customer testimonials with real names and photos are most credible. Specific statistics ('Join 47,293 marketers') outperform vague claims ('thousands of users'). Star ratings, media mentions, and industry awards also function as effective proof elements.

faq.question: Where should social proof be placed in an email?
faq.answer: Place social proof near the call to action — this is where doubt peaks and credibility matters most. A testimonial just above the CTA button can tip hesitant readers into clicking. Also use company logos or subscriber counts in the email header for instant authority.
